0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 13 December 1984, after the draft finalized by the Cosmetics Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council.
Over the years, 0.2 This Indian Standard was first published in 1973. the Sectional Committee decided to based on the experience gained, revise this standard and also prepare a separate product specification covering requirements of henna powder. 0.3 Adequate data are not available in literature on the phy>irochemical characteristics of henna powder and its methods of analysis. The Sectional Committee has prepard this standard on the basis of available information and experience gained during analysis of samples of henna powder. 0.4 In this revision, additional tests have been included to minimize the Tests for quantitative estimation of colouring chances of adulteration. pigment lawsone in henna powder based on spectrophotometric analysis; determination of moisture and volatile matter and fineness have also been included. 0.5 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard
lays down the methods of test for henna powder.

4. DETERMINATION MATTER OF MOISTURE AND VOLATILE

4.1 Procedure - Weigh accurately about 5 g of the prepared sample material in a moisture dish, about 6 to 8 cm in diameter and about 2 to 4 cm in depth. Dry in an air oven at a temperature of 105 rf 2�C to constant mass ( within f 5 mg ). 4.2

5. DETERMINATION

OF COLD

WATER

EXTRACT

5.1 Procedure - Weigh to the nearest 0.001 g, about 2 g of the prepared sample. Transfer the material quantitatively with water to a IOO-ml volumetric flask and fill to the mark with cold water. Stopper the flask and shake at approximately 30 minutes intervals for 8 hours and allow to settle for another 16 hours without shaking. Filter the Reject first few millilitres, then extract through a dry filter paper. evaporate a 25-ml aliquot to dryness in a tared dish on the water-bath Record the final and heat in the oven at 100 + 2�C to constant mass. mass.

6.2 Procedure - Weigh accurately about 2.5 g of the prepared sample. Transfer the material into a one-litre flask. Take 200 ml of the dilute sulphuric acid in a beaker and bring to boil. Transfer the whole of the boiling acid to the flask containing material and immediately connect the flask with a water-cooled reflux condenser and heat, so that the contents Rotate the flask frequently, of the flask begin to boil within 1 minute. taking care to keep the material from remaining on the sides of the flask Continue boiling for exactly 30 and out of contact with the acid. minutes. Remove the flask and filter through fine linen ( about 18 threads to the centimetre ) or through a coarse acid-washed, hardened filter paper, held in a funnel, and wash with boiling water until the Bring some quantity of sodium washings are no longer acid to litmus. Wash the residue hydroxide solution to boil under a reflux condenser. on the filter into the flask with 200 ml of boihng sodium hydroxide solution. Immediately connect the flask with the reflux condenser and boil for exactly 30 minutes. Remove the flask and immediately filter Thoroughly wash the residue through the linen or through filter paper. with boiling water and transfer to a Gooch crucible prepared with a thin but compact layer of ignited asbestos. Wash the residue thoroughly first with hot water and then with about 15 ml of ethyl alcohol and with three successive washings of 15 ml of petroIeum ether each. Dry the Gooch crucible and contents at 105 f 1�C in an air-oven for 3 hours, cool and weigh. Repeat the process of drying for 30 minutes, cooling and weighing until the difference between two consecutive weighings is less than 1 mg. Incinerate the contents of the Gooch crucible in the muffle Cool furnace at 550 I~I 20�C until all the carbonaceous matter is burnt. the Gooch crucible containing the ash in a desiccator and weigh. 5

7. DETERMXNATXON

7.1 Procedure - Weigh accurately about 5 g of the prepared sample in a silica dish. Heat the dish at first on a low flame and then in a muffle furnace maintained at about 600�C. Cool in a desiccator and weigh. Repeat the process of heating, cooling and weighing until constant mass is obtained. Preserve the ash for test under 8. 7.2 Calculation Mineral matter, M2 x 100 percent by mass = MI where Ma = mass in g of the ash, and Ml = mass in g of the material -8. DETERMINATION 8.1 Reagent 8.1.1 Dilute Hydrochloric Acid approximately 5 N. OF ACID taken for the test. ASH

INSOLUBLE

8.2 Procedure - To the ash preserved in 7.1 add 25 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid ( 5 N ), heat on water-bath for 10 minutes, allow to cool and filter the contents of the dish through Whatman filter paper No. 42, wash the filter with distilled water till the washing is free from acid. Return the filter and residues to the dish. Keep it in oven to dry and ignite to free from carbon ( in muffle furnace to 600�C ). Cool the dish in desiccator and weigh. Repeat the process of igniting, cooling and weighing, until the difference between two successive weighings is less than one milligram. Note the lowest mass. 6

-1984

- Weigh 5 g of prepared sample and transfer to a 9.1 Procedure beaker. Add about 100 ml of carbon tetrachloride and mix the contents intimately and allow to settle. The supernatant liquid is decanted and the residue again stirred with another loo-ml portion of carbon tetrachloride. Transfer This process is repeated till it is freed of all vegetable matter. the residue to a tared silica dish, ignite and weigh to constant mass.
NOTE - That the residue has been freed from vegetable matter can be judged by the absence of formation of light leafy scum on inside of the beaker when carbon tetrachloride evaporates partially.

10. THIN LAYER CHROMATOGRAPHIC DETECTION OF EXTRANEOUS DYES ( TLC) iTEST FOR

10.1 Preparation of Plates - Mix 10 g of the silica. gel ( of TLC grade, particle size 10 to 40 pm ) with 20 ml of distilled water to make a Activate slurry and spread over glass plates to a depth of 250 microns. the plates for 30 minutes, by keeping in an oven maintained at 105�C. IO.2 Preparation of Sample - Extract about 0.1 g of the prepared sample with 5 ml of chloroform and apply one drop of the extract on the base line of the plate. 10.3 Development of Chromatogram - Keep the prepared plates in a jar containing a mixture of chloroform : methyl ethyl ketone : glacial acetic acid ( 5 : 4 : 1 ). Allow the solvent front to run up to 15 cm ( the time taken is about 3 hours ) at room temperature ( 25 to 30�C ). Observe the spots obtained, under ultra violet light. 7

10.4.2 For comparison, henna powder. 11. DETERMINATION

use a reference sample prepared from standard OF LAWSONE PIGMENT CONTENT

11.1 Outline of Method - The pigment is extracted and the lawsone content is determined by comparing the observed optical density ( measured calorimetrically ) with a calibration curve, relating optical density to various concentrations of P-hydroxy, 1-4-naphthoquinone. 11.2 Apparatus 11.2.1 Spectrophotometcr 490 nm. 11.3 Reagents 11.3.1 Sodium Bicarbonate Solution 11.3.2 2-Hydroxy, I-4-naphthoquinone 11.4 Procedure 11.4.1 Preparation of Standard Calibration Curve - Construct a calibration curve by dissolving known amounts of 2-hydroxy, I-4-naphthoquinone ( CloHsOs ) varying in concentration from 0 to 2 percent under the same condition as described in 11.4.2 below. 11.4.2 Weigh 2.0 g of the prepared sample. Transfer it to a 100~ml volumetric flask. Add 5 percent ( m/v ) solution of sodium bicarbonate Shake the contents of the flask every and make up the volume to mark. half an hour or so for about 8 hours. Allow to settle overnight, thereafter filter the solution through a filter paper and reject the first few millilitres. Take 10 ml of the filtrate in a 25-ml volumetric flask and dilute with distilled water up to the mark. Measure the optical density of this solution with a spectrophotometer at 490 nm. 11.5 Calculation - Refer to the calibration curve and determine the percent lawsone content of the sample from the curve. 8 5 percent ( m/v ). or Photoelectric Colorimeter with a filter of

AMENDMENT

11.4.1 Preparation of Standard Calibration Curve Prepare standard 0.1 percent stock solution of 2-hydroxy, l-4-naphthoquinone (C IoH603) by dissolving it in sodium bicarbonate solution, 5 percent (m/v). Pipette O ml (Blank), I ml, 2 ml, 3 mi, 4 ml and 5 ml of standard 0.1 percent stock solution in 100 ml volumetric flasks and dilute with sodium bicarbonate solution 5 percent, (ndv) up to the mark. Measure the optical density of these solutions having varying concentration from 0.0, 10, 20 to 50 ppm of 2-hydroxy, and construct a 1-4-naphthoquinone, at 490 nm with a spectrophotometer calibration curve. The stock solution should not be stored for more than one month. 11.4.2 Weigh 2.0 g of the prepared sample. Transfer it to a 100 ml volumetric flask. Add sodium bicarbonate solution, 5 percent (m/v) and make up the volume to mark. Shake the contents of the flask every half an hour or so for about 8 h. Allow to settle overnight. Thereafter filter the solution through a filter paper and reject the first few millilitres. Take IO ml of the filtrate in a 25 ml volumetric flask and dilute with 5 percent sodium bicarbonate solution up to the mark. Further take"1 O ml of this solution in a 100 ml volumetric flask and dilute with 5 percent sodium bicarbonate solution up to the mark. Measure the optical density of this solution with a spectrophotometer at 490 rim.'
